title: Ust'-Ishim man
summary: Ust'-Ishim man is a modern human male known from a thigh bone found in 2008 on the Irtysh River in western Siberia. Radiocarbon dating gives about 45,000 years ago, making it the oldest directly dated modern human outside Africa and the Middle East. His genome was sequenced in 2014 and carries long Neanderthal segments.

as_recorded.value: Bone about 45,000 years old; femur found in 2008

where.modern_name: Irtysh River bank near Ust'-Ishim, Omsk Oblast, Russia
where.historical_name: Irtysh River valley, western Siberia, no polity

importance.justification: Provides the oldest high-quality modern human genome, dating Neanderthal admixture and the human mutation rate.

sources.title: Genome sequence of a 45,000-year-old modern human from western Siberia (Nature, doi:10.1038/nature13810; copy hosted by Reich Lab, Harvard)

sources.author: Fu et al.

sources.title: Earliest modern human sequenced

reviewer_note: The find spot is uncertain (Fu et al.: exact locality unclear; the femur eroded from left-bank alluvium north of the settlement); the pin is the settlement per Wikidata with 20 km uncertainty. The date range is the calibrated radiocarbon interval, not a life span. Admixture timing differs between the MPG summary (50-60 ka) and the paper abstract (7,000-13,000 years before he lived).
